check.reason: The target is CVS and its corporate strategy: the integration rhetoric and the press-release culture. Patients are not mocked, and no individual, reporter or author is targeted. There are no invented numbers or quotes, and no death, children or violence. The take matches the real story, a split that reverses years of combining pharmacy and insurance. 'Amicable' and 'a second press release' are clearly framed as satirical expectation, not reported fact. The tone is dry and deadpan, with no emojis or hashtags. 'As regulators look on' is vague enough not to misstate the story.

pick.title: CVS Health to split, reversing years of deal-making to combine pharmacies and insurance
pick.headline: CVS Discovers Pharmacy and Insurer Were Never Meant to Be Together
pick.take: After years of assembling the pharmacy, the insurer and the clinics into one seamless entity, CVS will now take it apart as regulators look on. We expect the breakup to be amicable and the integration to be described as a strategic success, with the savings reinvested in a second press release.
